title: CAD Checks Are Becoming More Explicit; Proof Is Still Narrow
question: Which claims withstand scrutiny, and where are the evidence or interpretations in tension?
argument: The strongest current evidence supports frontier models as first-draft tools for editable 3D scenes and parametric CAD, not as substitutes for engineering validation. CAD benchmarks and simulation checks establish narrower properties—task completion, solid validity, visual correspondence, configured joints, and simulated grasps—while tolerances, manufacturability, and physical transfer remain untested or undisclosed. For technical leaders, the key distinction is not whether an agent produced an artifact, but which properties its workflow actually checked.
synthesis: The MIT-CDFG survey supplies the broad CAD evidence and explicitly identifies missing tolerance and manufacturability tests; NVIDIA’s walkthrough shows the more concrete but still simulation-bounded checks a CAD-to-robotics workflow can run; the podcast’s RobotWorld discussion illustrates why completion claims need execution-based graders and why simulated outcomes should not be generalized to physical deployment. Together, they indicate that verification is becoming part of the agentic geometry workflow, but the verification layer must be matched to the decision: kernel or simulation checks can qualify a draft for further work, not certify a manufactured part or real-world robot behavior.
limitations: The survey is an authors’ synthesis of public evidence, with runnable code in only 132 of 707 cases, while NVIDIA does not disclose an error rate, reproducible configuration, or physical-transfer result. The podcast transcript is automatic and its RobotWorld figures require confirmation against the underlying paper or audio before being used as precise performance estimates.

claims.statement: The survey reports that leading models average 85% on 100 FreeCAD benchmark tasks, while tolerance specifications and manufacturability have not been tested on physical parts.

claims.statement: The survey’s evidence base is primarily demonstrative rather than independently reproducible, because it says only 132 of 707 reviewed cases include runnable code.

locator.quote: We reviewed 1646 public posts across 707 cases and checked each claim against available code, videos and documentation. Only 132 cases include runnable code, so most capabilities below are demonstrated rather than independently reproduced.

claims.statement: NVIDIA describes a CAD-to-simulation workflow that checks an imported robot’s scale, parts, and appearance against references before configuring joints, collision geometry, and physical properties.
NVIDIA’s stated final checks are Isaac Sim foundation and grasp checks followed by a simulated grasp, lift, hold, move, and release sequence; these checks do not establish physical-world correctness.
The podcast transcript reports that five general-purpose models left 63 of 84 robot tasks unsolved and cautions that each model ran once per task with no human baseline.
